0x004.name: register_animation
0x004.desc: Registers an animation for a movement state (state name, .prs file) through the registrar 0x421B30 (DS1 +0x004 FUN_00448D20); Desert Storm II adds the states SCRIPTED_ANIM_1..5 (MSR_SCRIPTED_ANIM_n_START / _STOP in its MovementStateRules) that Desert Storm hasn't got.

0x00C.name: register_standard_anims_c
0x00C.desc: Registers one of the exe's built-in animation sets (state name, .prs file pairs through the animation registrar 0x421B30); FUN_0044B120; 0x00C / 0x010 skip it when [0x62F454]+0x13D0 = 1. Desert Storm has no such slot - its script host registers the standard set itself.

0x010.name: register_standard_anims_a
0x010.desc: Registers one of the exe's built-in animation sets (state name, .prs file pairs through the animation registrar 0x421B30); FUN_00444490; 0x00C / 0x010 skip it when [0x62F454]+0x13D0 = 1. Desert Storm has no such slot - its script host registers the standard set itself.

0x014.name: register_standard_anims_b
0x014.desc: Registers one of the exe's built-in animation sets (state name, .prs file pairs through the animation registrar 0x421B30); FUN_00445290; 0x00C / 0x010 skip it when [0x62F454]+0x13D0 = 1. Desert Storm has no such slot - its script host registers the standard set itself.

0x018.name: register_standard_anims_d
0x018.desc: One of the exe's built-in animation sets (FUN_00445190: stance + idle animations - STANDING_STANCE_WITH_PISTOL upright_relaxed_with_pistol.prs ...), like 0x00C-0x014.

0x020.name: register_goat_anims
0x020.desc: Registers the four goat animation states through the animation registrar 0x421B30 (DS1 +0x004 load_anim's code): GOAT_STANDING goat_stand.prs, GOAT_GRAZING goat_grazing.prs, GOAT_WALK goat_walk.prs, GOAT_DEATH goat_death.prs. Skipped like the other registrars when [0x62F454]+0x13D0 = 1.
0x020.lua_hint: DS1 has the same state names (anim table 0x5EDF28); DS1's Mission1/3/5a register them themselves: call DS1 +0x004 load_anim("GOAT_STANDING","goat_stand.prs") etc. for the 4 pairs, once per level (a second load of a state shows DS1's 'Attempt to load anim twice!' box).

0x030.name: register_defuse_nuke_anim
0x030.desc: Registers DEFUSE_NUKE = Upright_Defuse.prs through the registrar 0x421B30 (one pair).
0x030.lua_hint: DS1 +0x004 load_anim("DEFUSE_NUKE", "Upright_Defuse.prs") - DS1's Mission11a/11b do exactly this; the state exists in DS1.

0x034.name: load_sound_bank
0x034.desc: Loads a .sbk sound bank (e.g. "Mission1.sbk") through the sound manager (FUN_0055dd20(mgr, name, 1)) and returns the bank.

0x040.name: get_stream_id
0x040.desc: Looks up a speech/cutscene stream by file name ("OBJ_M1_1A.wav", "CS_INTRO_S01.psf"): ELF hash of the name, checked against the loaded stream table; returns the id or 0.

0x050.name: play_stream
0x050.desc: Stops the current stream and starts this one at full volume (FUN_0055f840); the load time is logged ("Lost time = %d") and up to 5000 ms of it is added back to both game timers so scripted timing does not jump.

0x060.name: play_music_cue
0x060.desc: Plays event `cue` of the level's music bank ([0x6182f0], loaded from <level>Music.sbk at level init), e.g. 0x17; mission end uses 0x19.

0x064.name: preload_stream_stub
0x064.desc: No-op on PC (xor eax,eax; ret). Training DLLs call it with .psf names - a console stream preload left as a stub.

0x068.name: unused_0x040
0x068.desc: Empty function (ret). Only Training DLLs call it, with varying arguments; does nothing on PC.

0x070.name: load_scene
0x070.desc: Loads the level scene .env (FUN_0040b580) incl. the loading screen texts.

0x074.name: load_map_image
0x074.desc: Loads the mission map image sheet ("GWMission1.img") into the map sheet [0x60EE20].

0x078.name: set_map_image
0x078.desc: Selects the image of the map sheet used as the level map ([0x6107C0]) and resets the map's world bounds to the level's bounds.

0x07C.name: set_map_bounds
0x07C.desc: Sets the world area the map image covers: size = max - min, origin = min (the code stores min.x as origin y too - y is unused by the map).

0x080.name: load_level_strings
0x080.desc: Loads the mission's text file ("M01Strs.loc") into the text catalog (FUN_004f56d0).

0x088.name: link_markers
0x088.desc: Adds an AI route link from marker `from` to `to` (FUN_00504550), and back when both_ways = 1.

0x08C.name: unlink_markers
0x08C.desc: Removes the route link from -> to (and to -> from when both_ways); if anything was removed the route set is flagged for recomputing (set +0x18 = 1).

0x094.name: clear_look_target
0x094.desc: Clears the soldier's watched object (soldier +0x2594 = 0) set by 0x6C.

0x098.name: set_look_target
0x098.desc: Sets soldier +0x2594 = target object; the soldier's update reads the target's position from it (head/aim tracking of another object).

0x09C.name: get_ladder_count
0x09C.desc: Number of ladders registered by the scene ([0x63C9B4]+0x2D0); scripts register the ladder-climb animations only when it is non-zero.

0x0A0.name: spawn_birds
0x0A0.desc: Creates an ambient boid flock (hloboid.c) of `count` (min 10) objects inside region `region`.

0x0AC.name: set_time_of_day_speed
0x0AC.desc: Sets how fast the hour advances (atmosphere +0x40, game seconds per real second).

0x0B0.name: set_timer_scale
0x0B0.desc: Sets the time scale (+0x28) of timer [0x63C954] (slow motion / speed-up of that clock). Only Mission7 calls it.

0x0BC.name: run_time_of_day_until
0x0BC.desc: Lets the hour advance until `hour`, then stops (atmosphere +0x44 = 1, +0x48 = hour).

0x0C0.name: get_time_ms
0x0C0.desc: Current game time in ms ([0x63C954]+0x10). Used for all script delays.

0x0CC.name: get_average_frame_time
0x0CC.desc: mov ecx,[0x680098]; jmp 0x4BE550 = fld [timer+0xAC]: the 30-frame average frame time (seconds) of timer [0x680098] (the timer time_passed 0x0D0 reads +0x10 from = DS1's [0x63C954]). Missions 07/08 multiply it (x3) for per-frame progress bars.
0x0CC.lua_hint: No DS1 slot reads it: return game.readf(game.read32(0x63C954) + 0xAC) (DS1 timer layout +0xA8 dt s, +0xAC 30-frame average).

0x0D0.name: time_passed
0x0D0.desc: 1 once the given game time (ms, from get_time_ms 0x0C0) is behind the clock [0x680098]+0x10 (cmp; sbb; neg), else 0 - the missions' deadlines.

0x0D4.name: get_waypoint_position
0x0D4.desc: Copies the waypoint's position into out and returns out (hidden struct-return argument first).

0x0D8.name: set_waypoint_next
0x0D8.desc: Sets the waypoint a unit walks to after this one (waypoint +0x18; -1 = end of path).

0x0E0.name: set_waypoint_wait
0x0E0.desc: Sets how long a unit waits on arrival at this waypoint (+0x1C, added to the arrival time; soldier +0x238 = end of wait).

0x0EC.name: set_object_field_2af4
0x0EC.desc: Writes object +0x2AF4. For soldiers it is a waypoint index (-1 = a random waypoint is picked; read in FUN_00413b30, apparently a spawn/respawn point); vehicles use the same offset as a count. Called for squad members with waypoint-like values.

0x0F0.name: is_unit
0x0F0.desc: Calls the object's vtable +8 (non-zero for soldiers/AI units - the game uses it to choose unit-only code paths); 0 if the id is unknown.

0x0F4.name: is_active
0x0F4.desc: 1 if the object is in play (+0xC bit 0); a living soldier listed with flag 1 in the zone object table (0x48) also counts as active.

0x0F8.name: is_in_play
0x0F8.desc: Object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); returns +0xC & 1 (in play), 0 for an unknown id. Plain twin of is_active (0x0F4) without the zone-table soldier rule. No DLL call sites found.
0x0F8.lua_hint: Exact: game.read32(obj + 0xC) & 1 on the DS1 object (DS1 object table [0x63C9A0], FUN_004CA660).
0x0F8.match: close: DS1 is_active also returns 1 for a living soldier listed with flag 1 in the zone object table

0x0FC.name: activate_object
0x0FC.desc: Brings an object into play (vtable SetActive(1) unless already in play) and records it in the zone object table.

0x100.name: deactivate_object
0x100.desc: Takes an object out of play (SetActive(0)) and records it in the zone object table.

0x104.name: activate_objects
0x104.desc: activate_object for each id in an int array (ids pointer, count).

0x108.name: activate_living_objects
0x108.desc: activate_object for each id in the array that is not dead (is_dead 0x100 = 0).

0x10C.name: deactivate_objects
0x10C.desc: deactivate_object for each id in an int array.

0x110.name: set_ai_flag_80000
0x110.desc: Sets or clears bit 0x80000 of soldier +0x284 (AI flags); meaning of the bit not identified (Mission3 truck sequence toggles it).

0x114.name: respawn_unit
0x114.desc: Respawns/resets the object (vtable +0x40; debug print "Respawning unit:%d") and marks it active in the zone object table. Very common in mission scripts.

0x118.name: set_team
0x118.desc: Changes the object's team (FUN_004c9ea0); a soldier moved to team 0 gets AI flag 0x400000 and the squad-to-player mapping is redone (e.g. the Emir joining).

0x128.name: get_object_position
0x128.desc: Copies the object's current world position (render instance) into out and returns out.

0x12C.name: get_object_base_position
0x12C.desc: Copies object +0x1FC (a second stored position; for soldiers one of the position copies, possibly the start/home spot) into out and returns out. Mission1 uses it where a table entry is an object id instead of a waypoint.

0x130.name: is_path_finished
0x130.desc: 1 if the unit has no current waypoint (+0x220 == -1), i.e. it reached the end of its waypoint path.

0x134.name: kill_object
0x134.desc: Kills/destroys a living object by dealing more damage than its health (soldier vtable +0x3C, vehicle/prop damage); killer = -1 for none.

0x138.name: stop_object_sound
0x138.desc: Object by id; alive (vtable +0xC) or not, stops every playing voice tagged with the object's sound tag +0x4C (0x4B35D0 on the sound manager [0x6800EC]).
0x138.lua_hint: DS1 has the same function but no slot: FUN_0055E090 thiscall(sound manager [0x63C9AC], tag) stops voices whose +0x60 = tag; tag = DS1 object +0x4C (the tag 0x7DC / 0x7E0 / 0x7E4 use), e.g. x86rt.call(0x55E090, {tag}, mgr).

0x13C.name: is_dead
0x13C.desc: 1 if the object is dead/destroyed (soldier class query 3, others health == 0) or the id does not exist.

0x144.name: is_down
0x144.desc: Units: vtable +0x44 state query; type-8 objects (training targets): +0x54 bit 2. Training scripts use it to check a shot target; probably 'knocked down / hit'.

0x148.name: get_current_waypoint
0x148.desc: Returns the waypoint the unit is walking to (+0x220).

0x14C.name: set_path
0x14C.desc: Starts the unit on the waypoint path beginning at `waypoint` (vtable +0x34); -1 clears it. Usually followed by set_ai_state.

0x150.name: set_ai_state
0x150.desc: Sets the unit's AI state (+0x2378, FUN_0049d870; 5/6 = combat states) and for 0/1 also the sub-state; for vehicles state 0 sets +0x2610.

0x154.name: get_ai_state
0x154.desc: Returns the unit's AI state (+0x2378), e.g. compared with 5.

0x158.name: set_attack_target
0x158.desc: Gives the unit a target object (+0x234, with the time at +0x2FC; ignored for same-team targets); 0/unknown target clears it.

0x15C.name: set_follow_leader
0x15C.desc: Links the follower to a leader object (+0x26A4, registers it in the follow list); used for the Emir (Mission2).

0x160.name: clear_follow_leader
0x160.desc: Unlinks the follower (+0x26A4 = 0); a follower in AI state 3/4 is set back to state 2. Mission11B uses it on Franklin before walking him to the nuke.

0x164.name: set_ai_manager_flag_a4
0x164.desc: Writes [0x62F424]+0xA4 = value (AI manager = DS1's [0x60EDA0]; null-checked). Read only in the follower/leader movement code (0x41DD4C: == 1 -> take a formation slot from 0x41D700 and route there; 0x41DEFA: non-zero -> followers placed on the formation offset table 0x60BFD0 around their leader +0x214). Probably a squad formation / follow-mode switch. Mission09 calls it once with 0.
0x164.lua_hint: DS1's AI manager has no such field in use - safe to ignore (the only call turns it off).

0x168.name: move_to_position
0x168.desc: Living soldier (type 1, health +0x58 > 0): route-to 0x434090(&pos inline, notify 1) and, when found, AI state 3 via 0x498560. Same code as DS1's.
0x168.match: close: DS2 sets AI state 3 where DS1 sets 4 - DS2 AI state numbers are DS1's minus one from 3 up (DS2 0x498560 treats 4/5 as the combat states, DS1 FUN_0049D870 5/6); behaviour the same

0x174.name: near_waypoint
0x174.desc: 1 if the object is within `distance` (cm, 3-D) of the waypoint.

0x178.name: get_distance_to_waypoint
0x178.desc: If the object exists and is in play (+0xC bit 0): 3-D distance (fsqrt) from its render-instance position (instance +0x30 -> +0x108 or 0x4D2520) to the waypoint position (0x4D9790 on [0x6800F0]); otherwise 100000.0 (0x5E4374). No DLL call sites found.
0x178.lua_hint: DS1 +0x0F0 get_object_position + +0x0A0 get_waypoint_position and compute the distance in Lua; return 100000.0 when the DS1 object's in-play bit (+0xC & 1) is clear or the id is unknown.

0x17C.name: end_waypoint_wait
0x17C.desc: Clears the unit's waypoint wait end time (+0x238 = 0) so it moves on at once.

0x180.name: waypoint_in_view_cone
0x180.desc: 1 if the waypoint lies within `degrees` of the object's facing (yaw 0x4CE0E0, angle test 0x4D6330). 7 DLL sites, e.g. (unit, wp, 45.0).

0x184.name: near_object
0x184.desc: 1 if the two objects are within `distance` (cm, 3-D) of each other.

0x188.name: near_object_or_dead
0x188.desc: 1 if `object` is dead (health <= 0) or within `distance` of `other` (else as near_object).

0x18C.name: near_position
0x18C.desc: 1 if the object is within distance (cm, 3-D, 0x4D62E0) of the position given by pointer; 0 for an unknown id. Mission10.

0x194.name: object_in_view_cone
0x194.desc: 1 if `other` lies within `degrees` of `object`'s facing (0x4CE0E0 + 0x4D6330, no line of sight); 0 if either id is unknown. Mission08 (o, other, 45.0).

0x19C.name: play_sound_at_object
0x19C.desc: Plays sound id from the object's own bank (obj+0x40) at its position (min distance = radius*0.25) and posts an AI noise event of that radius (FUN_0049cb20, 2000 ms) so nearby soldiers can hear it. Sites use 3000.0 / 300.0.

0x1A4.name: object_in_region
0x1A4.desc: True if the object's position is inside region n (sphere or box; FUN_004fc600 + FUN_004fc040). 134 sites.

0x1A8.name: deactivate_all_objects
0x1A8.desc: Walks every object (0x4CEB80 on [0x6800E0], team -1, callback 0x445D10, 1): except type 7, SetActive(0) (vtable +8), stops its tagged sounds if alive (0x4B35D0), and soldiers are recorded in the zone object table (0x4022E0(obj, 0)). 7 DLL sites. (Same call shape as DS1 +0x72C movie_restore_objects but a different callback.)
0x1A8.lua_hint: No DS1 walk slot: iterate the DS1 object table ([0x63C9A0]+0x30 array) and call DS1 +0x0C8 deactivate_object on each that is not type 7 (DS1's deactivate also records non-soldiers in the zone table); stop tagged sounds with FUN_0055E090 if it matters.

0x1AC.name: deactivate_enemies_in_region
0x1AC.desc: For teams 1 and 2 (soldier list kind 1, 0x4CD340): every soldier inside the region (0x515940 on [0x6800F8] + 0x5158E0; region -1 = all) that isn't type 7 is taken out of play: SetActive(0), tagged sounds stopped (0x4B35D0), recorded in the zone object table (0x4022E0(obj, 0)). Teams 0 and 3 untouched. 3 DLL sites.
0x1AC.lua_hint: Loop teams 1-2 (DS1 team lists / +0x46C next_team_object), test DS1 +0x15C object_in_region (skip for -1), call DS1 +0x0C8 deactivate_object. DS1 +0x3D4 kill_units_in_region is the nearest built-in but kills (teams 1-3).

0x1B0.name: team_in_region
0x1B0.desc: 1 if any living soldier (vtable +0xBC health > 0) of the team's active soldier list (0x4CD340(team, 1)) stands inside the region (0x515940 + 0x5158E0); 0 if the region is unknown. 5 DLL sites.
0x1B0.lua_hint: For the player team DS1 +0x3D0; for any team iterate its members (DS1 +0x46C next_team_object) with DS1 +0x15C object_in_region and DS1 +0x1CC is_dead.
0x1B0.match: close: DS1 squad_in_region is fixed to the player team and has no health check

0x1B4.name: get_health
0x1B4.desc: Returns the object's health (+0x54) if its vtable+8 check passes, else 0.0. Callers multiply by a constant (percentage).

0x1B8.name: get_max_health
0x1B8.desc: 0x440AB0: object by id, vtable+0xC check, 0x4962C0 = unit def type 1 -> [def+0xB0]+0x24 / type 2 -> [def+0x80]+0x24 (u16) as float, else 0.0.

0x1BC.name: damage_object_ignore_invulnerable
0x1BC.desc: If the object exists and is alive (vtable +0xC == 1): clears the invulnerable bit 0x800000 (+0x27C, 0x496110(0)) if set, calls TakeDamage vtable +0x4C(amount, attacker 0) (= DS1 vtable +0x3C), then sets the bit back. Mission06 (0, 50.0), Training04 (0xE0, health x k).
0x1BC.lua_hint: DS1 +0x5F4 make_vulnerable, +0x168 damage_object, then +0x5F8 make_invulnerable only if the soldier had the bit (read DS1 soldier +0x284 & 0x800000 first).
0x1BC.match: close: DS1 damage_object doesn't bypass the invulnerable bit (DS1 soldier +0x284 bit 0x800000)

0x1C4.name: set_field_2e0
0x1C4.desc: Writes obj+0x2E0 = value (FUN_0049e790, plain setter; meaning unknown). Only Mission1 (0x12E, 0).

0x1D4.name: has_tracked_targets
0x1D4.desc: 0x403630 on the object: 1 if any of its 3 tracked-target entries (+0x288, stride 0x18, first dword) is set, i.e. the AI is aware of an enemy; 0 for an unknown id. Mission03 (0x10, 0xBB), Mission04.
0x1D4.lua_hint: DS1 has the same function FUN_00405DD0 (entries at soldier +0x290, stride 0x18) but no slot: return 1 if any of DS1 obj+0x290 / +0x2A8 / +0x2C0 is non-zero.

0x1D8.name: set_idle_look_around
0x1D8.desc: Sets/clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x20000 (on by default in the ctor); it gates FUN_0049cf20, the random idle head/aim glances every 2-5 s. Mission7 only.

0x1DC.name: set_ai_enabled
0x1DC.desc: enabled=0 sets soldier +0x284 bit 0x40000000, 1 clears it (AI-off flag). FrontEnd turns it off for its actors, Mission1 for the A-10s; the prisoner release turns it back on.

0x1E0.name: set_ignore_orders
0x1E0.desc: Sets/clears obj+0xC bit 0x1000 = AI debug text 'IGNORING ORDER CHANGES': FUN_0049d870 refuses AI mode changes while it is set. Mission11B Franklin while walking him to the nuke.

0x1E4.name: set_never_excluded
0x1E4.desc: Sets obj+0xC bit 8 = AI debug text 'Never EXCLUDED': the soldier's AI keeps running even when it would normally be culled (far away / off screen). 45 sites.

0x1E8.name: clear_never_excluded
0x1E8.desc: Clears obj+0xC bit 8 (see 0x188): the soldier may be excluded from AI updates again.

0x1F0.name: set_target_scanning
0x1F0.desc: 0x495FA0(on, refresh): sets (on = 1) / clears soldier +0x27C bit 0x400 (threat scan gate), refresh calls 0x405E20 - Desert Storm's set_target_scanning +0x1A0 (its soldier +0x284).

0x1F4.name: set_ignore_distractions
0x1F4.desc: Sets/clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x80 = AI debug text 'IGNORING DISTRACTIONS!' (no reaction to noises / threats; damage-reaction code skips it). For a soldier (type 1) also refreshes squad state (FUN_00407dc0). 112 sites.

0x1F8.name: is_away_from_stored_position
0x1F8.desc: 0x4CE4C0 on the object (= DS1 FUN_004CA120): r = object +0x50 if > 0 else 1.0; returns 1 if flag +0xC bit 0x40 is set or the render-instance position is more than r from the stored position +0x34..+0x3C (DS1 +0x30..+0x38), else 0; 0 for an unknown id. Many AI callers in both exes; what the stored point and the flag mean is not known. No DLL call sites found.
0x1F8.lua_hint: From DS1 memory: inst = [obj+0x2C]; pos = inst+0xF4 (if [inst+0x1C8] == 0, else FUN_004CD890); r = [obj+0x50] if > 0 else 1.0; return 1 if ([obj+0xC] & 0x40) ~= 0 or |pos - obj+0x30| > r.

0x1FC.name: destroy_object
0x1FC.desc: Applies damage = health + 1 to the object (FUN_0041a3f0): kills / destroys it through the normal destruction path (messages, effects).

0x200.name: set_target_scanning
0x200.desc: Sets (on=1) / clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x400, which gates the threat/target scan FUN_00407550; refresh != 0 also calls FUN_00407dc0. Mission1 turns it off for captive Foley (0x1F, 0, 1) and on again on release.

0x204.name: set_health_fraction
0x204.desc: Sets health (+0x54) = max health (unit stats +0x88 +0x24) * fraction. Mission1: Foley 0.25.

0x208.name: is_moving_forward
0x208.desc: True if the soldier's movement state (+0x2674) is walking/running/kneel-walking/crawling forwards (states 7-0xC, 0x13, 0x14, 0x53). Training1 'Move forwards'.

0x20C.name: is_moving_backward
0x20C.desc: True if the movement state is a backwards one (0xD, 0xE, 0x15, 0x16, 0x54, 0x57, 0x58). Training1 'Move backwards'.

0x210.name: is_strafing_a
0x210.desc: True if +0x284 has bits 0x2000 and 0x4000 (strafing; 0x4000 probably the direction, left or right unknown). Training1 'Strafe left and right' checks 0x1B0 and 0x1B4.

0x214.name: is_strafing_b
0x214.desc: True if +0x284 has bit 0x2000 but not 0x4000 (strafing the other direction). Training1 strafe step.

0x218.name: is_turning_left
0x218.desc: True if the movement state is a turning-left state (5, 0x11, 0x51). Training1 'Turn left and right'.

0x21C.name: is_turning_right
0x21C.desc: True if the movement state is a turning-right state (6, 0x12, 0x52).

0x220.name: is_crouching
0x220.desc: True if stance +0x348 is 1 or 5 (crouched). Training1 'To crouch'.

0x224.name: is_standing
0x224.desc: True if stance +0x348 is 2 or 3 (standing). Training1's 'To stand back up' prompt goes with this check.

0x228.name: is_prone
0x228.desc: True if stance +0x348 == 0 (prone). Training1's 'To go prone' prompt goes with this check.

0x22C.name: is_dead
0x22C.desc: FUN_0042b160: health <= 0 (for an in-play object of a non-player team only once +0x2A08 + 180 s has passed). 54 sites, 'test eax; je'.

0x238.name: set_targetable
0x238.desc: 1 clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x200, 0 sets it = AI debug text 'Cannot be targetted' (enemies ignore him). Captives are made untargetable; release passes 1.

0x240.name: set_stick_to_waypoints
0x240.desc: Sets/clears obj+0xC bit 0x10 = AI debug text '** sticking to waypoints **': the soldier keeps to its waypoint path instead of chasing / taking cover.

0x248.name: scale_by_skill_task_time
0x248.desc: Object vtable +0x6C(3, value) (= DS1 soldier vtable +0x5C, FUN_00432F80): value x skill-table column 3 for the soldier's level (DS2 table 0x6350B8 + level*0x44, +0xC; level +0xDD4); 0.0 for an unknown id. Missions 07/08: progress -= dt x 3 / scale_by_skill(soldier, 1.0) - a skill-dependent task duration.
0x248.lua_hint: DS1 soldiers have the same virtual: x86rt.call(vtable[+0x5C], {3, value bits}, obj) -> ST0; or value * float at 0x619434 + level*0x44 (level = DS1 soldier +0x2A18, DS1 table 0x619428, 17 floats per level). The tables' columns may hold different numbers in the two games.

0x24C.name: set_min_alert_level
0x24C.desc: FUN_0049d250: alert floor +0x2DC = level (0-4) and raises the current alert +0x2D8 to it. 4 = combat (sends script message 0x04 for enemies).

0x250.name: set_alert_level
0x250.desc: FUN_0049d2b0: current alert +0x2D8 = level (not below the floor); level 4 on an enemy sends message 0x04 'reached combat alert'.

0x254.name: get_alert_level
0x254.desc: Returns alert level +0x2D8 (0-4; Mission3 compares with 4 = combat).

0x260.name: set_ai_flag_20
0x260.desc: Sets soldier +0x284 bit 0x20 (class query vtable+0x4C(0xC) returns it; read in target selection 0x404423 and weapon code 0x4A554D - possibly 'hold fire'). No clear call. Mission1 (0xC), Mission3 guards 0xF3-0xF6.

0x268.name: set_movement_locked
0x268.desc: Sets/clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x4000000; while set the movement code (0x426ADE, 0x45C1F8) ignores the player block's stick input. Training1/3 on the player soldier.

0x26C.name: stop_moving
0x26C.desc: Clears +0x2394 and applies movement rules MSR_AI_STOP_MOVING (0x1D) and MSR_ZERO_SPEED (3): the soldier halts.

0x270.name: set_stance_stand_walk
0x270.desc: FUN_0045cf00(2, 1) + default stance +0x380 = 2 (standing; the AI itself uses 2 near its destination - walk pace).

0x274.name: set_stance_stand
0x274.desc: FUN_0045cf00(3, 1) + default stance +0x380 = 3 (standing, the AI's normal/run stance). 167 sites.

0x27C.name: set_stance_crouch_alt
0x27C.desc: FUN_0045cf00(5, 1) + default stance +0x380 = 5 (crouched variant, also counted as crouching by 0x1C0).

0x284.name: set_can_pursue
0x284.desc: vtable+0x78 = sets/clears soldier +0x284 bit 0x100 (getter vtable+0x7C); without it the AI won't advance on its target (FUN_0049df90 holds, mode 6). Mission1 Foley 0 while captive, 1 after.

0x290.name: face_waypoint
0x290.desc: Turns the soldier to face waypoint n (waypoint list [0x63C9B0], 0x20-byte entries; angle FUN_004BB100 -> facing target +0x374).

0x294.name: turn_by
0x294.desc: Sets the facing target +0x374 to the current rotation (+0x208) with yaw + degrees (wrapped 0-360). Mission3: 180.0.

0x298.name: award_experience
0x298.desc: 0x4743B0(points) on the object: points scaled by difficulty ([0x680128]+4: 0 x0.9, 1 x1.0, 2 x1.1, 3 x1.2), rounded, added to experience points +0xDE8 with promotion (nothing at level 9, +0xDD4).
0x298.match: close: DS1 FUN_00434190 has no 4th difficulty (x1.2); otherwise identical

0x29C.name: set_experience_level
0x29C.desc: Sets experience/rank level +0x2A18 clamped 0-9 (FUN_0042d1b0; 'Experience level' in AI debug).

0x2A0.name: raise_experience_level
0x2A0.desc: Sets the experience level to level only if the current one (FUN_0042d150) is lower.

0x2AC.name: line_up_at_waypoint
0x2AC.desc: Lines the soldier up on the waypoint's position (0x4D9790) and rotation (0x4D97A0) with 0x473DD0(&pos, &rot, distance, 1, 1) - the line-up DS1's pick-lock path uses (DS1 FUN_00433330(pos, rot, 100.0, 0, 0)), here without a movement rule and with both trailing flags 1. Mission04 (unit, wp, 100.0).
0x2AC.lua_hint: No plain DS1 slot: x86rt.call(0x433330, {&pos, &rot, distance bits, 1, 1}, obj) (thiscall ret 0x14) with pos / rot from the DS1 waypoint table (FUN_004D13F0 / FUN_004D1400 on [0x63C9B0]); nearest slots DS1 +0x244 pick_lock_at_waypoint (adds rule 0x4C) or +0x66C place_at_waypoint_rotated (teleport).

0x2B4.name: mount_vehicle
0x2B4.desc: Vehicle 0x490E80(soldier, &seat, &x) finds a free seat (DS1 FUN_0043CFD0), then soldier 0x482ED0(vehicle, seat, x, 0, 0) mounts (DS1 FUN_00433F00). 21 DLL sites, e.g. Mission02 (8, 0x185). The catalogue's compare_objects_490e80 was this.

0x2B8.name: mount_vehicle_seat
0x2B8.desc: Mounts the soldier into the given seat of the vehicle (soldier, vehicle, seat) - not DS1 +0x24C (any free seat).

0x2BC.name: is_in_vehicle
0x2BC.desc: True if the soldier's current vehicle (+0x267C) has script id vehicle.

0x2C4.name: get_user_of
0x2C4.desc: vtable+0xA0 (soldier class: +0x26A4) -> script id of the linked object (e.g. who is using a vehicle / mounted gun), -1 if none. Training3 compares with the player (0x79) or -1.

0x2C8.name: set_skin_texture
0x2C8.desc: Registers the texture (FUN_0054a0b0) and makes it the render instance's skin override (FUN_00503290); flag 1 also stops all animations of the instance (FUN_00502bb0, caged prisoners). E.g. 'AlliedPOW.bmp'.

0x2CC.name: stamp_time_2a10
0x2CC.desc: If class query vtable+0x4C(0x11) is true, writes the current game time (ms) to +0x2A10. Training1 30 sites before waits; meaning unknown.

0x2D0.name: set_calm
0x2D0.desc: Sets soldier +0x284 bit 0x400000 ('calm': quiet speech) and +0x2A00 = 0. Training3 per soldier.

0x2D4.name: wave_on
0x2D4.desc: Movement rule MSR_WAVE_ON (0x5C): the soldier plays the wave-on gesture.

0x2E4.name: cower
0x2E4.desc: Movement rule MSR_COWER (0x5E); if it applies, plays sound 0x143 from the soldier's bank (radius 1000).

0x2EC.name: start_gas_choke
0x2EC.desc: For a soldier (type 1; no null check on the id) applies movement rule 0x68 = MSR_GAS_CHOKE (DS2 MOVEMENTSTATERULES) through vtable +0x80 (= DS1's vtable +0x70 rule call). DS2-only rule.
0x2EC.lua_hint: DS1 has no gas-choke rule / animation: no-op, or DS1 +0x52C play_scripted_animation with a choke .prs if one gets ported.

0x2F8.name: scripted_anim
0x2F8.desc: Movement rule MSR_SCRIPTED_ANIM_<n>_START (0x6A + n - 1) or, with start 0, _STOP (0x6F + n - 1), n 1-5: plays the animation registered for SCRIPTED_ANIM_<n> (register_animation 0x004). Desert Storm has no such states - its play_scripted_animation +0x52C does the job.

0x2FC.name: set_movement_state
0x2FC.desc: 0x47B150(state) on the object (= DS1 FUN_0042D240): sets the movement state +0x688 (DS1 +0x2674) with its transition side effects. No DLL call sites found. DS2 state numbers come from DS2's MOVEMENTSTATERULES (139 states) and differ from DS1's.
0x2FC.lua_hint: x86rt.call(0x42D240, {ds1_state}, obj) (thiscall ret 4) after mapping the state by name from DS2's MOVEMENTSTATERULES.TXT to DS1's.

0x300.name: stretch
0x300.desc: Movement rule MSR_STRETCH (0x6A), idle stretch animation.

0x30C.name: disembark_vehicle
0x30C.desc: Movement rule MSR_DISEMBARK_VEHICLE_LEFT (0x68) if nonzero, else _RIGHT (0x69).

0x310.name: start_scripted_unconscious
0x310.desc: Applies movement rule 0x5A MSR_SCRIPTED_UNCONCIOUS (DS2 MOVEMENTSTATERULES); was named start_defusing_nuke.

0x314.name: stop_scripted_unconscious
0x314.desc: Applies movement rule 0x5B (recover from MSR_SCRIPTED_UNCONCIOUS); was named stop_defusing_nuke.

0x318.name: set_combat_ready
0x318.desc: Bundle: stance stand (0x435640(3,1) + default stance +0x380 = 3), never excluded (+0xC |= 8), clears DS2 soldier flag +0x105C bit 0x40000, minimum alert 4 (0x498500), ignore distractions off (0x497DD0(0)), and for a soldier AI state 5 (0x498560; DS2 5 = DS1 6, combat). 77 DLL sites.
0x318.lua_hint: DS1 sequence: +0x20C set_stance_stand(o), +0x188 set_never_excluded(o), +0x1E4 set_min_alert_level(o,4), +0x198 set_ignore_distractions(o,0), +0x114 set_ai_state(o,6) (DS1 numbering); the +0x105C flag has no DS1 field.

0x31C.name: set_patrol_mode
0x31C.desc: Bundle: minimum alert 4 (0x498500), stance stand (0x435640(3,1) + +0x380 = 3), stick to waypoints (+0xC |= 0x10), ignore distractions on (0x497DD0(1)), never excluded (+0xC |= 8). 22 DLL sites.
0x31C.lua_hint: DS1 sequence: +0x1E4 set_min_alert_level(o,4), +0x20C set_stance_stand(o), +0x1DC set_stick_to_waypoints(o,1), +0x198 set_ignore_distractions(o,1), +0x188 set_never_excluded(o).

0x320.name: reset_soldier_state
0x320.desc: Calls soldier vtable+0x70(0x5F) then re-applies its movement state (+0x2674) via FUN_0042d3a0(state, 0); exact effect unclear (Mission6 only).

0x324.name: freeze_animations_except_weapon
0x324.desc: Like freeze_animations (0x328): every entry of the render instance (+0x30: count +0x1B4, array +0x1B8, 0x14 B) whose model is set (0x565BB0) gets 0x565FA0(0) (DS1 FUN_00503760(0)) - except the entry on the held weapon's connector (held item vtable +0x84, def +0x24 category 5 -> index 0x55DC40(def +0x94)). No null check on the id. Mission06 (0x34, 0x42, 0x3D, ...).
0x324.lua_hint: Loop DS1 instance [obj+0x2C] entries (+0x214 count, +0x218 array, 16 B) and call FUN_00503760(0) on each with a model (+8) except index FUN_00502C30(def+0x94 hash) of the held weapon (DS1 vtable +0x74); or simply DS1 +0x298.
0x324.match: close: DS1 freeze_animations also freezes the held weapon's entry

0x328.name: freeze_animations
0x328.desc: Switches off every animation layer of the object's render instance (FUN_00502bb0); nothing restarts them (Mission 1 caged Foley).

0x32C.name: stop_spine_anim_layers
0x32C.desc: Switches off the animation layers on the 'BIP01 SPINE1 / SPINE2 CONNECTOR' bones (upper-body layers).

0x330.name: stop_hat_anim_layer
0x330.desc: Switches off the animation layer on the 'BIP01 HAT CONNECTOR' bone (head layer).

0x334.name: stop_face_anim_layer
0x334.desc: Switches off the animation layer on the 'BIP01 FACE CONNECTOR' bone.

0x338.name: strip_inventory
0x338.desc: Removes the soldier's inventory items (FUN_00431830(0); category-8 / special items kept).

0x33C.name: say_speech_4e
0x33C.desc: Soldier (type 1, no null check) speaks speech-bank event 0x4E from its own bank: 0x480170(0x4E, 0x4E, 0, 0, 0, 1, bank 0 = soldier +0x40, 0) (DS1's speech FUN_004366D0 with two more arguments: bank and one flag). Mission07 x4 (after a +0x8A4 check).
0x33C.lua_hint: No DS1 speech slot: DS1 +0x7DC play_sound_at_object(o, 0x4E, bank = read32(obj+0x40), 1000.0) plays the event from the soldier's bank (without the busy / dead / quiet rules).

0x340.name: say_speech
0x340.desc: Soldier (type 1, no null check) speaks a speech-bank event: 0x480170(event, event, 0, 0, flag, 0, bank, flag2); bank 0 = the soldier's +0x40. Mission04 (o, 3, 1, 0, 0), Training01 (0xD7, 0xD59, 0, 0, 0).
0x340.lua_hint: DS1 +0x7DC play_sound_at_object(o, event, bank or read32(obj+0x40), 1000.0); for the full rules call DS1's speech FUN_004366D0 (thiscall, 6 args, ret 0x18) with x86rt.call.

0x344.name: get_kill_count
0x344.desc: For a soldier (type 1, no null check): +0xF64 (vehicles destroyed, ++ after the 'destroyed' speech at 0x491618) + +0xF60 (soldiers killed this mission, ++ in the kill credit at 0x4964DB); else 0. (0x348 returns +0xF60 alone.) No DLL call sites found.
0x344.lua_hint: DS1 keeps the same counters: return read32(obj+0x2C84) + read32(obj+0x2C88) (DS1 mission kills ++ at 0x49C7FA, vehicles at 0x43E394; summed the same way at 0x499CB7).

0x350.name: is_holding_laser_designator
0x350.desc: Object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); for a soldier (type 1) whose held item (vtable+0x84 = DS1 +0x74) has definition category ([def+0] via item+0x24) 0x12 = LASER DESIGNATOR (category parser 0x4506C0) returns 1, else 0. Mission10 polls it for units 0x65 / 0x67 / 0x78.
0x350.lua_hint: DS1 uses the same category number (0x12 = LASER DESIGNATOR, parser 0x493CA0): soldier = object by id (FUN_004CA660 on [0x63C9A0]); type ([obj+4]) == 1; held = vtable+0x74(); held and [[held+0x24]+0] == 0x12.

0x354.name: vehicle_fire_at
0x354.desc: Orders a vehicle to fire weapon slot n (+0x260C list) at the target object once: sets +0x2640 target, +0x2644 slot (same as the debug key 'Fire vehicle weapon').

0x358.name: set_ai_flag_40000000
0x358.desc: Sets (on) or clears soldier +0x27C bit 0x40000000 - Desert Storm's soldier +0x284 bit 30, which its +0x180 sets.

0x360.name: set_ai_flag_200000
0x360.desc: Sets / clears bit 0x200000 of the soldier's AI flags (+0x284). Meaning of the bit not identified.

0x364.name: set_ai_flag_200000_all
0x364.desc: Sets / clears AI flag bit 0x200000 (+0x284) on every soldier of all 4 teams, except units of class 0xB.

0x368.name: vehicle_is_occupied
0x368.desc: 0x48B800 on the object: seat count = byte [[unit+0x24]+0x80]+0x40 (vehicle def), occupant array [obj+0x680]; 1 if any seat pointer is non-null, else 0. No type check (vehicles only). Mission04.
0x368.lua_hint: api[0x80C](veh) ~= -1, or exact: seats = byte [[[obj+0x24]+0x80]+0x40], occupants [obj+0x2608] (DS1), any non-null.
0x368.match: close: DS1 get_vehicle_driver returns the first occupied crew seat's script id or -1 (crew seats from the driver seat on); DS2 checks every seat and returns 1/0

0x36C.name: damage_team_in_region
0x36C.desc: Damages every soldier of the team standing in the region by damage_per_second x frame dt (vtable+0x3C); called per frame for kill zones.

0x370.name: damage_team
0x370.desc: Every active object of the team (0x4CD340(team, 1), next +0x18) takes damage_per_second x frame dt (dt from timer [0x680098] 0x4BE550) through vtable+0x4C(amount, 0) (= DS1 TakeDamage vtable+0x3C; DS2 soldier vtables are DS1's +0x10). Note the float comes FIRST. Mission07 (per frame, teams 2 / ebx).
0x370.lua_hint: Loop the team's active list (FUN_004C9720([0x63C9A0], team, 1), next +0x14) and call soldier vtable+0x3C(dps*dt, 0); or api[0x2BC] with a region covering the level.
0x370.match: close: DS1 damage_team_in_region(region, dps, team) only hurts members inside a region; DS2 hurts the whole team

0x378.name: show_object
0x378.desc: Clears render-instance flag 0x10000000 (+0x2C -> +0xC) = object drawn again (Mission 1 init uses it on zone pieces).

0x37C.name: hide_object
0x37C.desc: Sets render-instance flag 0x10000000 (+0x2C -> +0xC) = object not drawn.

0x384.name: fire_weapon
0x384.desc: Object by id -> 0x4A0060(obj, 0, 0, 0) thiscall on itself (trigger pull with the weapon as its own shooter; ret 0x10, null-shooter check = DS1 FUN_004A1AD0). Mission01 / 04 fire placed weapons (ids 0xFC, 0xA7, 0xA8).

0x390.name: call_strike
0x390.desc: Queues a timed strike at a position (one of 10 slots of [0x60EDA4], 8000 ms, posts event 0x6F; target -1 = none); network MP sends it via FUN_004636f0. Probably the air / mortar strike (Training2 air-strike lesson).

0x394.name: give_magazines
0x394.desc: Adds magazines x magazine size (def +0x92) to a weapon item's reserve rounds (skipped in grenade-launcher mode).

0x398.name: weapon_is_empty
0x398.desc: 1 when the item (or a soldier's held weapon) has no rounds left (magazine +0x80 + reserve +0x54 = 0).

0x39C.name: clear_weapon_state
0x39C.desc: Zeroes weapon item fields +0x74, +0x84, +0x88 (fire / reload timers?); Training1 only.

0x3A0.name: detonate_explosive
0x3A0.desc: Object by id; if its definition ([obj+0x24]) is category 5 (weapon) and class +0xC0 is 7 (frag grenade) or 0x11 -> 0x49A890(0,0,0): explosion event in the explosion manager [0x680118] (0x4D7020; flags 0x35B0A, class 0x11 0x2DB0A + 60.0) with def +0xD4 / +0xD8 (u16) as damage / radius at the item's position, object removed (0x4CDE50), script message 0x18 (explosion). Mission03 detonates 0x79 / 0x7A / 0x7B.
0x3A0.lua_hint: DS1 0x804 explosion_at_position(x, y, z, zone_object, radius, damage) with the item's position (obj+0x30) and its weapon def +0xD4 / +0xD8 (same fields DS1's weapon code passes at 0x4A1A73), then deactivate the item (api 0xC8).

0x3A8.name: enable_env_sound
0x3A8.desc: Turns an environment (ENVSND) sound slot on, restoring its volume (sound manager slot, stride 0x34).

0x3AC.name: disable_env_sound
0x3AC.desc: Turns an environment (ENVSND) sound slot off.

0x3B0.name: set_env_sound_volume
0x3B0.desc: Sets an enabled environment sound slot's volume (0..1, e.g. 0.05, 1.0).

0x3B4.name: play_sound
0x3B4.desc: Plays a sound id from a sound bank, non-positional (2D), min distance 1000.

0x3B8.name: play_sound_at
0x3B8.desc: Plays a sound id from a bank at a world position (x, y, z passed inline), min distance 1000.

0x3BC.name: clear_sound_queue
0x3BC.desc: Empties the scripted sound / speech sequence queue (count [0x617C50] = 0).

0x3C0.name: queue_sound
0x3C0.desc: Appends a sound to the sequence queue (max 12); position used when positional = 1, speaker -1 = none.

0x3C4.name: play_sound_queue
0x3C4.desc: Starts the queued sound sequence (FUN_0055de90); 1 when the queue was not empty.

0x3C8.name: debug_print
0x3C8.desc: Bare ret (0x4031A0) - no-op; missions pass a sprintf buffer.

0x3D4.name: key_down
0x3D4.desc: 1 while a keyboard key (DirectInput scan code, 2..9 = keys 1..8) is down; scripts use it for debug shortcuts behind debug_mode_enabled.

0x3E4.name: set_player_soldier
0x3E4.desc: Hands an active object to every player's view controller (FUN_00472cb0): camera / control switch to it.

0x3E8.name: camera_shake
0x3E8.desc: Starts a camera shake on every viewport camera (e.g. 25.0, 0, 2000.0); ignored while one is running.

0x3EC.name: camera_shake_at
0x3EC.desc: Camera manager [0x680120] 0x4DD2A0: for every active camera (flag 1, not already shaking 0x40; stride 0x1B4) whose eye (+0x28) is closer than radius to the position, starts a shake with strength x (1 - dist/radius), param2, duration (0x4DD220 -> 0x4DD1A0, the same starter DS2's camera_shake 0x3E8 uses). Mission02 / 06: (pos, 2000.0, 10.0, 0, 400.0).
0x3EC.lua_hint: d = distance(player 1 camera or soldier position, position); if d < radius then api[0x32C](strength*(1-d/radius), param2, duration_ms).
0x3EC.match: close: DS1 camera_shake(strength, param2, duration_ms) shakes every camera with full strength; DS2 adds position + radius fall-off

0x3F4.name: pause_zone_tracking
0x3F4.desc: While set, (de)activations don't update the per-zone rosters ([0x617DD0]); scripts wrap their zone streaming in 1 ... 0.

0x3F8.name: zone_of_object
0x3F8.desc: World zone index of the object's model (+0x1C -> +0xC8 -> +0x1BC); -1 if none.

0x3FC.name: get_zone_objects
0x3FC.desc: Returns the zone's roster: pointer to {object id, enabled} pairs and their count (0 for a bad index).

0x400.name: count_zone_active
0x400.desc: Number of the zone's roster objects currently in play (object +0xC bit 0).

0x404.name: count_zone_enabled
0x404.desc: Number of the zone's roster objects marked enabled (the scripts' 'grunts' count).

0x408.name: restore_zone_objects
0x408.desc: For each {id, enabled} roster entry: enabled -> activate (soldiers resumed), else deactivate. Used when a player enters a zone.

0x40C.name: suspend_zone_objects
0x40C.desc: Records each roster object's in-play state, then deactivates it. Used when no player is in the zone.

0x410.name: zone_activate_one
0x410.desc: Keeps one roster object active in the player soldier's zone: drops *current if it left / died, else picks an enabled, idle, living one (FUN_00484640) and activates it; *current = its id or -1.

0x418.name: count_living_grunts
0x418.desc: Counts enabled, living roster objects in all zones; with 0 only those whose +0x267C is 0.

0x41C.name: set_max_spawned
0x41C.desc: Sets the spawn system's maximum ([0x617DC0], default 9) - the scripts' 'capacity'.

0x428.name: set_spawn_flag_617dd4
0x428.desc: Sets spawn-system flag [0x617DD4] (1 after init_spawn_points); meaning unclear.

0x430.name: get_spawn_point
0x430.desc: Pointer to a spawn point record (0x1C bytes: +0x10 state 0 off / 1 on / 2 permanently off, +0x14 counter). Scripts read / bump the fields directly.

0x434.name: enable_spawn_point
0x434.desc: Turns the spawn point on (state 1); a permanently disabled one only with force (logs 'Enabling spawn point').

0x438.name: enable_spawn_point_when_clear
0x438.desc: Spawn manager 0x631848 (records 0x40 B at +0x2C) 0x44E320(index): only for a point in state 0 or 1, and only if none of the current wave's units (lists +0x24[+0x1C], count +0xC) is still alive / in play (0x446D70); then state 2 (on), counter +0x2C = 0, script message 0x4C if it was state 0, log 'Enabling spawn point:%d'. DS2 spawn states: 0 never enabled, 1 off, 2 on, 3 permanently off. 173 call sites.
0x438.lua_hint: Check the point's previous units are dead before api[0x378](index, 0) (DS1 spawn record from api 0x374, 0x1C bytes).
0x438.match: close: DS1 enable_spawn_point(index, force) has no 'units still alive' check and no message; DS1 states are 0 off / 1 on / 2 permanently off

0x43C.name: force_enable_spawn_point
0x43C.desc: 0x44E2A0(index, 1): force-enables one spawn point (was named disable_all_spawn_points).

0x440.name: disable_spawn_point
0x440.desc: 0x431130 on 0x631848: ignored for state 3; permanent -> state 3 + script message 0x4D, else state 1; then objective re-evaluation 0x436340 and the log '%sisabling spawn point:%d' ('Permanently d' / 'D') - the same strings as DS1.

0x448.name: push_dynamic_object_at
0x448.desc: Object type 2 with dynamics flag +0x64 = 1: dynamics +0x68 -> 0x520BD0(force, offset): wakes the Karma body (+0x48), adds force x 0.01 at body position + offset x 0.01 (cm -> m) via 0x5BA460 (add force at position). Mission03 once.
0x448.lua_hint: api[0x8C8](obj, force, 0.01) (offset ignored); exact: dynamics [obj+0x64] FUN_00512480(force, 0.01, world position + offset).
0x448.match: close: DS1 push_dynamic_object(object, direction*, strength) adds direction x strength at the body centre (no offset, no 0.01 factor); DS1's internal FUN_00512480 does take an absolute position (3rd arg) the slot passes as 0

0x44C.name: freeze_dynamic_object

0x5AC.name: activate_objective
0x5AC.desc: 0x436620: only for state 0: popup of record +0x14 for 5 s (0x443820) + sound 0xCD4 (when +0x14 != -1), state = 1, display entry +0x4C gets flags |= 0xA (shown + tracked, 0x440390 = DS1 show_objective), auto types 0/1/2/6 re-evaluated at once (0x436340). The old name 'complete_objective' was wrong. DS2 objective records live in the mission data manager 0x631848 (the same object that holds the spawn points): records at [0x63189C] (= mgr+0x54), 0x54 bytes each, count mgr+0x58. Record: +0 result when achieved (0 mission success: script message 0x11, or campaign end_mission(2) when no script; 1 mission failure after +4 ms: mgr+0x5C = now + delay, then message 0x12 / end_mission(1) (0x436C90); 2 activate record +0xC; 3 deactivate record +0xC and mark ITS display entry done), +4 delay ms, +8 type (0/1/2/6 are evaluated automatically by 0x436340; 3 = composite, achieved when all records in list +0x3C/+0x40 are state 2, 0x4362B0), +0xC other record index, +0x10 achieved text hash, +0x14 activated text hash, +0x18 STATE (0 inactive, 1 active, 2 achieved), +0x30/+0x34 script-id list for the auto types, +0x3C/+0x40 sub-record list, +0x4C display index (byte, -1 none) = the campaign objective entry [0x62F454]+0x12E8 list (entry layout identical to DS1's [0x60EDC0]+0x12E4 list: +0 index byte, +0x14 flags, +0x18 12 marker positions, +0xA8 12 marker objects, next +0xD8). Display flags DS2 uses: activation |= 0xA (shown+tracked, 0x440390), achievement = (flags & ~8) | 4 + sound 0xCD4 (0x440520) - exactly DS1's bits 1|2|4|8. There is NO failed state or failed flag: a 'failure' objective is a record whose result is 1. Records are level data, not created through the API (DS2 has no add_objective slot).
0x5AC.lua_hint: Lua keeps state[i]; if state[i] == 0: state[i] = 1, api[0x4B8](display[i]) (+ popup / sound if wanted). display[i] = the record's +0x4C from the DS2 level's objective data.
0x5AC.match: close: DS1 show_objective(display index) only sets flags |= 0xA; DS2 also keeps a record state, pops up the record's text and plays 0xCD4

0x5B0.name: objective_is_active
0x5B0.desc: Record state ([0x63189C] + i*0x54 + 0x18) == 1 (activated, not yet achieved). Old name 'objective_is_complete' was wrong.
0x5B0.lua_hint: state[i] == 1 from the Lua objective table (DS1 0x4D0 get_objective_state only reports display flags shown/done).

0x5B4.name: complete_objective
0x5B4.desc: 0x4366B0: ignored while a delayed mission end is pending (mgr+0x5C) or already state 2; state = 2, popup of record +0x10 (5 s), display entry +0x4C = (flags & ~8) | 4 + sound 0xCD4 (0x440520 = DS1 complete_objective), script message 0x4F (record index), composite check 0x4362B0, then by result +0: 0 message 0x11 / end_mission(2), 1 delayed failure (mgr+0x5C = now + record +4 ms -> message 0x12 / end_mission(1)), 2 activate record +0xC, 3 deactivate record +0xC and mark its display entry done. Old name 'fail_objective' was wrong: there is no failed state.
0x5B4.lua_hint: if not pending_end and state[i] ~= 2: state[i] = 2; api[0x4C0](display[i]); then result: 0 -> api[0x48C](2) (DS2 sends the script message 0x11 instead when a script exists), 1 -> timer then api[0x48C](1), 2 -> activate(other), 3 -> state[other] = 0 + api[0x4C0](display[other]).
0x5B4.match: close: DS1 complete_objective(display index) does the display part (flag 4, untracked, sound 0xCD4); the record state, popup text, message 0x4F and the result chain need Lua

0x5B8.name: objective_is_complete
0x5B8.desc: Record state == 2 (achieved). Old name 'objective_is_failed' was wrong.
0x5B8.lua_hint: state[i] == 2; DS1 0x4D0 get_objective_state(display, &shown, &done) gives done = flag 4 if only the display matters.

0x5BC.desc: 0x436290: an ACTIVE record (state 1) goes back to 0 (inactive). Display flags are not touched. Old name 'reopen_objective' was wrong (it does not undo a completed one).
