0x610.name: queue_call
0x610.desc: Timed callback queue (the cutscene / overview builder). Pushes a type-6 event on the event queue [0x63C978] (FUN_004db6b0): after delay_ms (float, milliseconds from now) the game calls the DLL function callback(event*), which reads arg1 at event+0x34 and arg2 at event+0x38 and calls ONE ordinary API slot with them. Events queued while the cinematic bit is set get flags 0x1E (skippable: +0x560 runs them at once). There are no command codes - the 'command' is whichever API slot the callback wraps; see 'commands' (API slot(s) the callback calls: number of the 2783 queue_call sites).

commands.0x7C0+0x110/0x114: look up object, then move/route it (164; +0x110/+0x114 alone: 52)
commands.0x034: unknown (126; callback is itself a DLL function pointer arg)
commands.0x66C: place at waypoint with its rotation (118)
commands.0x540: fade out to colour (113; arg1 = ms int, arg2 = colour 0xAARRGGBB)
commands.0x53C: fade in from colour (112; arg1 = ms int, arg2 = colour)
commands.0x52C: play scripted animation / back to default (111)
commands.0x560+0x4FC+0x4F4+0x534+0x584+0x51C+0x59: cutscene end chain: run queued calls, camera off, letterbox off, AI on, input on, movie end (30)

0x614.name: set_player_control
0x614.desc: Turns player input on/off for every player block (block +0x34); off parks each block's soldier in 0x617C40 and detaches it, on reattaches it. Used around cutscenes.

0x61C.name: load_animation
0x61C.desc: Loads (or finds already loaded) a .prs animation by file name through the anim manager [0x63C968] (FUN_00500a40); returns the handle used by +0x52C / +0x654.

0x624.name: play_scripted_animation
0x624.desc: Plays a loaded animation on a soldier as scripted movement state 0x4B (anim mode 3); anim 0 returns the soldier to the default movement state (the one set by +0x670).

0x628.name: letterbox_on
0x628.desc: Starts the cinematic letterbox bars (view controller [0x63C98C] FUN_004d1d00(1); skipped with dev flag u).

0x634.name: fade_in
0x634.desc: Screen fade from a solid colour (0-255 per channel) back to the picture over duration_ms (view controller FUN_004d2c70, mode 1). Queued at the start of each cutscene shot.

0x638.name: fade_out
0x638.desc: Screen fade from the picture to a solid colour over duration_ms (FUN_004d2cd0, mode 0); (0, 0,0,0) clears. Queued at the end of each cutscene shot.

0x63C.name: take_control
0x63C.desc: Makes every player block drive the given soldier (view 0 camera saved in 0x5ED118 and switched, block soldier = object, camera mode 1) - scripted 'player takes control' moments.

0x640.name: release_control
0x640.desc: Undoes +0x544: block soldier cleared, control mode 2 (AI drives), saved camera restored.

0x644.name: select_item_by_name
0x644.desc: Makes a soldier hold the inventory item whose definition name matches (e.g. "US_WPN_M16A2") (FUN_0042ec10).

0x674.name: set_combat_speech_muted
0x674.desc: 0x4424F0: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x1000000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Set = the soldier says no AI speech: the gates of the spotted-enemy callouts 0x406030 (0x20/0xBB2 infantry, 0x534/0xC92 ...), 0x406950 (0x4F7/0x852), 0x480ED0, 0x481B40, 0x483290, 0x483460 all return when it is set. Mission01 sets it on the squad (ids 0, 6, 7, 8) around scripted scenes and clears it afterwards.
0x674.lua_hint: DS1 has no per-soldier mute: set_idle_chatter (0x1D0, obj, 0) stops only idle chatter. Full emulation needs a plugin hook on DS1's speech FUN_004366D0 (thiscall soldier) that skips listed soldiers; otherwise ignore (cosmetic).

0x678.name: set_acts_badly_wounded
0x678.desc: 0x442430: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x40000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Set = AI treats the soldier as badly wounded whatever his health: 0x409720 runs its < 30 %-health branch (0x496710 retreat / call-for-help request, 1500 ms, 2500.0) when it is set, the player 'help a downed soldier' check 0x4757A0 skips him, and with bit 0x2000000 (+0x680) the running movement set becomes RUNNING_PANIC (0x47B450, movement table 0x6118F8 mode 5). Slot 0x318 clears it. Mission02 sets it with +0x680 on id 0x82 (a civilian / hostage).
0x678.lua_hint: No DS1 equivalent (DS1 AI has no wounded-retreat flag). Ignore, or approximate panic by ordering the soldier to run to a waypoint (DS1 0x110 set_path + run stance).

0x67C.name: reset_soldier_to_idle
0x67C.desc: 0x4425E0 -> 0x47DF60 (only caller): if the movement state +0x6A0 is a firing / aiming state (7, 0x1B, 5, 6, 0x1A) 0x45A9A0(1); stops every sound tagged with the soldier (+0x4C) and with its held item (0x4B35D0 on [0x6800EC]); clears targets (+0x250/+0x258 moved to +0x254/+0x25C and zeroed, +0xDC8 = 0, +0x27C &= ~0x1000, +0x139C &= ~0x200), new random chatter time +0x460, movement state 0 + flag +0x105C bit 0 cleared, default animation restarted on the render instance (+0x30). Mission01/02/03/06/08 call it on every squad member right after movie_start (0x6B0) - puts actors into a clean idle pose for a cutscene.
0x67C.lua_hint: DS1 pieces: stop_firing (0x580), stop_moving (0x204), reset_soldier_state (0x294); DS1 reset_all_soldiers (0x88C, FUN_00489E40) does the target clearing (+0x258/+0x260) + held-item release for EVERY soldier - x86rt-call its per-soldier part or just 0x580 + 0x204 per actor.

0x680.name: set_panic_run
0x680.desc: 0x442470: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x2000000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Only read at 0x47B4CB: together with bit 0x40000 (+0x678) a soldier ordered to run uses movement state 0xE4 = RUNNING_PANIC (movement table 0x6118F8 [state*0x2A + mode], mode 5) instead of the normal run (mode 3 -> 4 limping run when health < 30 %). Mission02: 0x678(0x82, 1) + 0x680(0x82, 1).
0x680.lua_hint: DS1 has no RUNNING_PANIC state - ignore (soldier runs normally).

0x684.name: set_keep_weapon
0x684.desc: 0x4424B0: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x20000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Set = no automatic weapon choice: the AI weapon selector 0x45AB80 (from the soldier update 0x488697; picks the best weapon for the target via 0x45A0F0 and switches with 0x45A9A0) returns at once. Missions set it with +0x690 after start_firing (0x694) so a scripted gunner keeps the weapon he was given (Mission02 ids 0x5C / 0x84, Mission03).
0x684.lua_hint: No DS1 flag. DS1's AI weapon switching is different; usually harmless to ignore. If a scripted gunner swaps weapons, re-hold the item each frame (DS1 0x5CC hold_item).

0x688.name: set_fire_at_will
0x688.desc: 0x442530 -> 0x471C20 thiscall(soldier, on): on sets +0x27C bit 0x1000 (= DS1 +0x284 bit 0x1000) and, when the soldier holds nothing (vtable +0x84), draws the best weapon (0x45A9A0(1)); 0 clears the bit. Same code as DS1 FUN_00424750 (or dh,0x10; vtable+0x74; FUN_004A5930(1)) used by the squad order toggle FUN_00404D70 (DS2 0x404680) - the fire-at-will / hold-fire order. Mission03 toggles it on ids 0x21/0x23/0x24.
0x688.lua_hint: DS1 has the identical function but no slot: x86rt call 0x424750 thiscall (ecx = soldier object from FUN_004CA660 on [0x63C9A0]) with arg on.

0x68C.name: set_stance_locked
0x68C.desc: 0x442560: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x8000000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Set = the AI stance chooser 0x435EC0 (via 0x436240 per soldier update) skips its target-distance branch: no automatic crouch when the target is within 800 cm (0x435640(1, 1)) and no random stance change every 5 s (0x475EF0). Stance itself = +0x348, setter 0x435640(stance, flag). Mission03 once.
0x68C.lua_hint: No DS1 flag: re-apply the wanted stance each update with DS1's stance / GruntMode slots.

0x690.name: set_hold_trigger
0x690.desc: 0x4425A0: object by script id (0x4CF4F0 on [0x6800E0]); on != 0 sets, 0 clears bit 0x10000 of soldier +0x105C (a DS2-only soldier flag word; DS1's AI flags +0x284 are DS2's +0x27C). Set = the AI fire control 0x406700 never releases the trigger: without a target it normally calls 0x49A4A0 (weapon +0x68 = 0) at 0x406933 - skipped when the bit is set (0x40692A); 0x406540 (keep-spraying decision, = DS1 FUN_00408410) returns 0. Used after start_firing (0x694) with +0x684 for scripted suppressive fire (Mission02 0x5C / 0x84, Mission03), cleared before stop_firing.
0x690.lua_hint: DS1: call start_firing (0x57C) for the soldier every frame while the flag is on (DS1's AI releases the trigger otherwise), stop with 0x580.

0x694.name: start_firing
0x694.desc: Pulls the trigger of the soldier's held weapon (weapon vtable+0x3C: +0x64 = 1, burst count for mode 2) and plays the fire stance (FUN_00427420(4)).

0x698.name: stop_firing
0x698.desc: Releases the trigger of the soldier's held weapon (FUN_004a4a30: weapon +0x64/+0x68 = 0).

0x69C.name: resume_ai
0x69C.desc: End-of-cutscene resume: sets the AI-enabled bit 0x1000000 (soldier +0x284) on all soldiers via [0x60EDA0] and clears the global no-damage flag 0x60F25C.

0x6A0.name: freeze_ai
0x6A0.desc: Cutscene freeze: clears the AI-enabled bit 0x1000000 on all soldiers and sets the global no-damage flag 0x60F25C (counterpart of +0x584).

0x6A4.name: movie_cancel_pressed
0x6A4.desc: Cutscene skip query: 1 when any player pressed MOVIE_CANCEL (action 0x36), with fade + [0x618348] = 1 as side effect (also 1 with dev flag u).

0x6A8.name: movie_cancel_held
0x6A8.desc: Same query as +0x58C without side effects.

0x6B0.name: movie_start
0x6B0.desc: Starts a cinematic (sets cinematic bit [0x63C948]+0x1B8C bit 0).

0x6BC.name: clear_battlefield
0x6BC.desc: 0x4428F0: resets the 0x33C-byte entries of [0x68011C] (0x4F8AA0), clears all projectiles ([0x6800E4] 0x4F3F80), re-initialises the 0x4C-byte effect / explosion entries of [0x6800B8] (0x4E18C0), removes the corpses of the corpse manager [0x641614] (0x46EE10: 6 holders -> vtable+8(0); same manager as 0x904), stops every playing non-reserved voice (0x4B3550 on [0x6800EC]) and sets view controller [0x6800CC] +0x74 = 0. Called right before movie_start in Missions 1/2/3/6/8 (cutscene start cleanup).
0x6BC.lua_hint: DS1 FUN_00486EB0 does the same job (effects, projectiles, decals, corpses, particles, explosions, emitters - it is what DS1 movie_end 0x598 / reset_world_state 0x884 call): x86rt call 0x486EB0 (no args), then 0x6C0 set_view_controller_74(0). Note it also stops DS1 emitters; sounds are not stopped (DS1 0x34 stop_stream only stops the stream).

0x6C0.name: movie_end
0x6C0.desc: Ends a cinematic; sends script message 0x12 after the overview.

0x6C4.name: link_convoy
0x6C4.desc: Links vehicles into a convoy chain: vehicle follows 'ahead' and leads 'behind' (-1 = none; +0x2C28/+0x2C2C/+0x2C30), gap in cm (2000/3000 seen). Mission 4 trucks, Mission 8.

0x6C8.name: set_speed
0x6C8.desc: Sets a vehicle/aircraft speed factor: max +0x2C38 and current +0x2C34 (0.25-5 seen).

0x6D4.name: set_door_key
0x6D4.desc: Registers a key item for a locked door (table [0x60EDA8], entries {key, door, -1}); using the key unlocks the door (flag 8). Mission 1: cooler keys 0x46 -> 0x25.

0x6D8.name: give_item
0x6D8.desc: Adds an existing item object to a soldier's inventory (AddItem FUN_004314d0).

0x6DC.name: take_item
0x6DC.desc: Removes an item object from a soldier's inventory (FUN_004318a0).

0x6E4.name: remove_medikits
0x6E4.desc: Sets the soldier's category-8 item (MediKit) count to 0 and holsters it if held.

0x6E8.name: set_medikit_uses
0x6E8.desc: The soldier's first category-8 item (MediKit; 0x47D250 walks the 25 inventory slots at +0x6D4) gets its count +0x58 = uses (0x49D280; a carried kit's holder +0x78 too); with 0 and the kit held (vtable +0x84) the soldier stops holding it. Training03 on Bradley 0x79.

0x6EC.name: has_item
0x6EC.desc: True when the soldier carries the item object (FUN_00437200).

0x6F0.name: medikit_count
0x6F0.desc: Count of the soldier's category-8 item (MediKit; owner +0x2DA0 / item +0x54).

0x6F4.name: is_holding
0x6F4.desc: True when the soldier's held item (vtable+0x74) has this script id.

0x6F8.name: hold_item
0x6F8.desc: Makes the soldier hold the inventory item with this script id; -1 = holster. 1 on success, 0 if not carried.

0x6FC.name: hold_medikit
0x6FC.desc: Makes the soldier hold its category-8 item (MediKit); 0 if it has none.

0x700.name: set_player_soldier
0x700.desc: Gives player n control of the soldier (block soldier = object, remembered in 0x617C40).

0x708.name: get_item_position
0x708.desc: Writes the object's world position (render instance) and its zone (+0x1C).

0x710.name: place_item
0x710.desc: Activates an item, moves it to a position/zone and refills it (count 1, rounds reset) - Training 2 respawns an item with it.

0x714.name: air_strike_active
0x714.desc: True while any of the 10 air-strike slots in [0x60EDA4] is running (state +8 = 1).

0x724.name: make_invulnerable
0x724.desc: Sets the soldier's invulnerable bit 0x800000 (+0x284) - cutscene actors.

0x73C.name: disable_ai
0x73C.desc: Clears the soldier's AI-enabled bit 0x1000000 (+0x284); +0x60C sets it.

0x740.name: show_tutorial_text
0x740.desc: Formats a catalog text (printf with the following arguments, e.g. control names from +0x618) into the tutorial/objective bar 0x617DE8; ignored in split screen.

0x744.name: get_control_name
0x744.desc: Returns the text of the keys/buttons bound to a control (index into 0x5D9338 -> action id), for tutorial text.

0x760.name: face_object
0x760.desc: Turns a soldier to face another object (head bone for soldiers).

0x764.name: face_position
0x764.desc: Turns a soldier to face a world position.

0x768.name: attack_target
0x768.desc: Forces a soldier's AI target (adds it as known enemy, message 0x34) and locks fire on it (+0x2564/+0x2568 = 1).

0x76C.name: clear_attack_target
0x76C.desc: Releases the forced target / fire lock of +0x63C.

0x770.name: aim_at_target
0x770.desc: Sets a forced target without the fire lock (+0x2568 = 1 only) - soldier aims/tracks.

0x780.name: dismount
0x780.desc: Makes a soldier leave the vehicle / mounted gun it is on (+0x267C, FUN_0042e850).

0x784.name: play_animation_mode
0x784.desc: Like +0x52C but anim mode 4 (flag set) or 6 (flag 0) - probably loop vs play-once; anim 0 does nothing.

0x788.name: night_vision_on
0x788.desc: Turns the night-vision view effect on for all views (sound 0x4BE).

0x78C.name: night_vision_save_and_off
0x78C.desc: 0x44A090: for the 4 view controllers [0x6800D0..0x6800DC] stores the night-vision flag (vc +0x6C) in 0x634384[i] and turns NV off (0x4DA880(0, ...) with the NV sound 0x4BE / 0xBE6), same for the main view controller [0x6800CC] -> 0x634380. Counterpart 0x790 restores the saved states (the existing catalogue maps 0x790 to DS1 night_vision_off - it is a restore). Called at cutscene start after movie_start / clear_battlefield.
0x78C.lua_hint: Save DS1 view controllers [0x63C990..0x63C99C] +0x6C (NV flag) yourself, then call 0x65C; for 0x790 call 0x658 if any saved flag was 1 (DS1 0x658 turns it on for all views).
0x78C.match: close: DS1 night_vision_off turns NV off for all views but saves nothing

0x790.name: night_vision_restore
0x790.desc: Restores the night-vision state 0x78C saved (DS1 has no saved state: left off).

0x798.name: set_reserved_soldiers
0x798.desc: Stores a reserved soldier count (0x6182FC) used by +0x668.

0x79C.name: get_reserved_soldiers
0x79C.desc: Returns the reserved soldier count (DS1 keeps it at 0x6182FC, set by +0x664).

0x7A0.name: free_soldier_slots
0x7A0.desc: 0x445500 -> 0x44E630 on 0x631848: 16 - reserved count ([0x631888], set by 0x798) - soldiers in the active lists of teams 0-2 (0x44E600: 0x4CD340(team, 1), next +0x18). Room left for spawning. (The catalogue's 0x79C free_soldier_slots is really get_reserved_soldiers: it just returns [0x631888].) Mission01/02/05 test it before spawning.

0x7A4.name: place_at_waypoint_rotated
0x7A4.desc: Teleports an object to a waypoint and turns it to the waypoint's stored rotation (cutscene actor placement).

0x7A8.name: set_default_movement_state
0x7A8.desc: Sets the default movement state (MovementStateRules table [0x60EC80]) that +0x52C(object, 0) returns soldiers to.

0x7AC.name: light_on
0x7AC.desc: Turns a scene light on: sets flag 4 on light entry (index & 0xFF) of the Lights.cpp manager [0x63C95C] (+8 array, 0x108 B each). Lights without flag 4 contribute nothing (0x51E176).

0x7B0.name: light_off
0x7B0.desc: Turns a scene light off (clears flag 4 of the light entry in [0x63C95C]). Mission 1 switches lights 0x15/0x14/0x10/0x0D off after its intro film.

0x7B4.name: set_light_on
0x7B4.desc: 0x443590 -> 0x5499E0 on the lights manager (renderer [0x680038] +0x419E4; entry (index & 0xFF) x 0x164 B, flags +4): on sets flag 4, 0 clears it - one call for light_on (0x7AC = (light, 1)) / light_off (0x7B0 = (light, 0)). Mission06 switches lights 0x16-0x2E with it.
0x7B4.match: close: DS1 has separate slots - 0x674 light_on when on != 0, 0x678 light_off when 0

0x7BC.name: set_light_colours
0x7BC.desc: 0x4435D0: both colours to float RGBA (0x5486E0), then 0x549C10(light, &a, &b, fade) on the lights manager: with fade > 0 and a fader (entry flag 0x40) blends towards colour_b (fader +0xE4, 0x548930, flag 0x80); else writes colour_b into the D3D light's diffuse (+0x38+4) and ambient (+0x38+0x24) and SetLight. Same structure as DS1 FUN_0051D3F0. Mission07.
0x7BC.match: close: DS1 writes colour_a to ambient and colour_b to diffuse; DS2 uses colour_b for both (colour_a unused in the code read)

0x7E8.name: show_message
0x7E8.desc: Looks up a catalog text (0x4F6730) and shows it in the bottom pop-up bar (FUN_004d33a0 on view controller [0x63C98C]) for the given ms (all sites 5000).

0x7F0.name: debug_printf
0x7F0.desc: 0x4031A0: bare ret - debug print, no-op in the shipped exe (Mission07 passes 'Released Tank!\n').

0x7FC.name: emitter_start
0x7FC.desc: 0x44A230: entry (index & 0xFF) x 0x108 B of the emitter list [0x62F46C] +4 -> 0x4F2D60: flags +0x70 |= 1, timer +0x50 = +0x54, +0 = +4, +0xF8 = 0, +0x104 = 0, then 0x4F1840. Same as DS1 FUN_004F31F0 (entries 0x7C B there). NOTE: the catalogue's 0x800 'emitter_start' is the stop (0x4F0C00 clears +0x70 bit 0 and stops the emitter's sound +0x104) = DS1 0x6C8.

0x804.name: emitter_stop
0x804.desc: Stops emitter n of [0x60EDD8]: clears flags +0x70 bit 0 and +0x74.

0x808.name: set_attack_target
0x808.desc: Clears the soldier's 3-entry target list (+0x290), puts target in it (FUN_00407040, may send message 0x34 'enemy spotted'), makes it the current target (FUN_00406390), sets +0x2564/+0x2568 = 1, +0x2B60 = 0 and +0x29D8/+0x29DC = value. Only called from cutscene-queue callbacks.

0x80C.name: add_attack_target
0x80C.desc: Like 0x6CC but keeps the existing target list: adds target, makes it current, +0x2568 = 1, +0x29D8/+0x29DC = value.

0x818.name: soldier_signal_action
0x818.desc: FUN_00408990 on the soldier: plays movement-state action 9 (or animation 0x4D via vtable+0x70); if one played, plays sound 2 of the bank of vtable+0x74's object at the soldier and posts a 500-unit AI hearing event; returns 1, else 0. Exact action unknown (gesture/shout?).

0x824.name: play_object_anim
0x824.desc: Plays an animation on a non-soldier object whose model is a hierarchy (model type 4, e.g. vehicles/props): FUN_00501c20(slot 0, anim, flag, 0, 3.0). anim 0 stops it (the movie clean-up uses it that way).

0x828.name: show_zone
0x828.desc: Makes a world zone visible: clears flag 4 (hidden) on zone +0xC (FUN_004d1230). Zone pointer from 0x704. Mission 2 shows its BMP1WRECK / LIMO_BODY_DAMAGED zones with it later in the mission.

0x82C.name: hide_zone
0x82C.desc: Hides a world zone: sets flag 4 on zone +0xC (FUN_004d1220; the same flag object removal sets); null-safe. Mission 2 uses it at set-up on the wreck / damaged zones.

0x830.name: find_zone
0x830.desc: Finds a world zone by name (hash FUN_004b9ab0 compared with zone +0x210 in the world's zone list [0x63C948]+0x1A48, next +0xB0); returns the zone pointer or 0.

0x844.name: camera_zoom_in
0x844.desc: Jumps to FUN_00444330: steps the current player's camera FOV in (zoom), clamped to the held weapon's zoom limit, with the scope zoom sound - the zoom key handler.

0x854.name: show_movie_text
0x854.desc: Looks up a level text by hash in the mission string table (FUN_004f5e80) and adds it, line by line, to the subtitle/text box of view n ([0x60ED14+n*4], FUN_00508ed0); shows 'WARNING : MISSING MOVIE TEXT' if absent.

0x858.name: reset_view_effects
0x858.desc: Calls 0x4FCD10 on both view controllers ([0x62F364], [0x62F368]) - screen effect reset.

0x85C.name: movie_restore_objects
0x85C.desc: Movie clean-up over all objects (callback 0x486860): cutscene actors (instance flag 0x20000) get their animation stopped and are deactivated; objects the movie start hid (flag 0x40000, see 0x7D8) are reactivated.

0x860.name: set_sky
0x860.desc: Applies a loaded .sky record (from 0x734) to the atmosphere: FUN_004e2be0 sets sky, fog colour and fog distances (+0x40/+0x44 -> atmosphere +4/+0xC) and the far clip.

0x864.name: load_sky
0x864.desc: Loads a .sky file (e.g. 'Mid_day_sunny.sky') into the next free sky slot and writes the slot pointer to *out (for 0x730).

0x868.name: init_skies
0x868.desc: Allocates count sky slots (0x84 B each) for 0x734; called before loading skies (count 2 in Missions 1/4/8/9).

0x870.name: set_view_tint
0x870.desc: View controller [0x62F364 + view*4] 0x4FCCA0({r, g, b, 1.0}) - a screen colour.

0x878.name: get_player_count
0x878.desc: Returns the number of local players (input blocks, [0x610798] & 0xFFFF); scripts test > 1 for split screen.

0x87C.name: set_movie_version
0x87C.desc: Records the movie/cutscene data version ([0x5ED11C], first call wins); warns 'We have different movie versions used together' if another one was set. All sites pass 9.

0x880.name: get_movie_version
0x880.desc: Returns the movie version set by 0x7BC; the cutscene command code branches on > 5.

0x884.name: set_vehicle_free
0x884.desc: Vehicles only (object type 0): false sets vehicle flag +0x2CD8 bit 2, true clears it; the bit is passed to the vehicle dynamics (+0x2C20/+0x2C24, FUN_005192b0/0x51a350) - looks like a brake/hold. Used by cutscene command callbacks.

0x88C.name: show_briefing
0x88C.desc: Switches the front end to state 0x14 = the mission briefing popup.

0x890.name: play_sound_at_object
0x890.desc: Plays a sound id from a bank (FUN_0055de20) at the object's position, tagged with the object (+0x4C) so 0x7E4 can test it; distance e.g. 1000.0 / 10000.0.

0x894.name: play_object_sound_at_position
0x894.desc: 0x447AF0: sound manager [0x6800EC] 0x4B5870(bank, sound, position, min_distance, object's sound tag +0x4C, 7) - like play_sound_at_object (0x890) but at a given point, still tagged with the object so object_sound_playing (0x8A4) sees it; then 0x515470(9, object, sound, 0) and, for a soldier, 0x475370 + lip sync 0x47D500(anim): anim = lipsync_anim, else the lip-sync table entry for the sound (0x43FDE0, filled by 0x9D4), else the default talk anim (0x5641E0(1) on [0x6800A4]). Mission02 (2 calls).
0x894.lua_hint: DS1 0x7DC plays at the object; for a point call DS1's sound play directly: x86rt thiscall 0x55DE20 (ecx = [0x63C9AC]; args bank, sound, position ptr, min_distance, [object+0x4C]) - the same call 0x7DC makes, so 0x7E4 still works. Lip sync: none on DS1.

0x898.name: play_object_sound_2d
0x898.desc: Plays a sound id from a bank non-positionally (no position, distance 0), tagged with the object's sound tag (+0x4C).

0x89C.name: play_object_sound_if_quiet
0x89C.desc: 0x447C10: returns at once while a sound tagged with the object is playing (0x4B2B70 on [0x6800EC] = object_sound_playing); else plays at the object's position (render instance +0x108 / 0x4D2520) like 0x890: 0x4B5870(bank, sound, pos, min_distance, tag +0x4C, 7) + soldier lip sync (as 0x894); no 0x515470 event. Sites pass distances 1000-10000 (e.g. (0x21, 0x990, bank, 10000.0, 0)). 15 sites in Missions 2/3/4/6/8/10, Training 2/4.
0x89C.lua_hint: if api[0x7E4](obj) == 0 then api[0x7DC](obj, sound, bank, min_distance) end
0x89C.match: close: DS1 play_sound_at_object has no 'only if quiet' check and no lip sync - test 0x7E4 object_sound_playing first

0x8A0.name: play_object_sound
0x8A0.desc: Unless the object's voice channel (+0x4C) is playing (0x4B2B70 on the sound manager [0x6800EC]): plays sound id from bank on that channel (0x4B5870(bank, sound, 0, 0, channel, 0xF)); for a soldier also 0x475370 and the lip sync (0x47D500 with the line's length; flag 0 -> length from the bank). Desert Storm's closest: play_sound +0x2F8 (bank, sound), not positional.

0x8A4.name: object_sound_playing
0x8A4.desc: 1 while any sound tagged with this object (+0x4C) is still playing (FUN_0055e130), else 0. Scripts wait on it before the next line.

0x8AC.name: kill_with_anim
0x8AC.desc: Kills the soldier: damage = 2 x health (+0x54) via vtable+0x3C, then vtable+0x70(anim) plays the given animation/state (death animation).

0x8B0.name: kill_soldier
0x8B0.desc: FUN_0042b1b0: health +0x54 = 0, damage 1.0 via vtable+0x3C, death time backdated 180 s (+0x2A08) - instant death / corpse. Used in loops over soldier lists.

0x8B8.name: viewfinder_on
0x8B8.desc: Shows the camcorder-style viewfinder overlay ([0x618418] = 1) used in mission overviews.

0x8C0.name: set_sound_mode
0x8C0.desc: Sound manager FUN_0055f270(mode, 1): requests sound context 'mode' (+0x14 = 1 when it differs from the current +0x10). Called with 1 before MovieStart and 0 when the movie/briefing ends - movie vs game sound mode.

0x8CC.name: explosion_at_position_flags
0x8CC.desc: 0x443CD0: explosion manager [0x680118] 0x4D7020(&pos, zone 0, radius, damage, 0, 0, flags, 0, 0, 0) - like 0x8C8 (= DS1 0x804, zone from an object, fixed flags 0x25B0A) but without a zone object and with caller flags (sites: 0x61B02, radius 400.0, damage 100.0). Missions 2/3.
0x8CC.lua_hint: api[0x804](x, y, z, <any object in that zone, e.g. the player soldier>, radius, damage); or x86rt thiscall 0x4E92C0 (ecx = [0x63C9D0]; &pos, zone, radius, damage, 0, 0, flags, 0) - DS2 flag bits may not mean the same on DS1, 0x5B0A is the safe value.
0x8CC.match: close: DS1 0x804 needs a zone object (its +0x1C) and uses fixed flags 0x5B0A

0x8D4.name: get_vehicle_driver
0x8D4.desc: Returns the script id of the first occupied crew seat of a vehicle (FUN_0043d440: seat flags +0x260C / occupants +0x2608, starting at the driver seat), or -1.

0x8D8.name: show_text_screen
0x8D8.desc: Draws a full-screen page with the catalog text and 'press any key' (FUN_0040b1e0, background colour) and blocks until a key / button / mouse press (FUN_00539a20(0)).

0x8E0.name: hash_name
0x8E0.desc: Returns the engine's name hash (FUN_004b9ab0, lower-case LFSR as used for zone / texture names).

0x8E4.name: set_vehicle_flag_10
0x8E4.desc: Vehicle: on sets +0x2CD8 bit 4 (0x10) and +0x2E8 = 360.0, +0x2EC = 180.0 (full angle ranges, probably turret / sight arcs); off clears the bit. When set and the vehicle is stopped its dynamics inputs are zeroed (0x43A14C).

0x8F0.name: movie_freeze_world
0x8F0.desc: Pauses timer [0x63C954] (FUN_004ba560(0)) and points the camera manager's clock at the main timer [0x63C958]; with 1 also hides (render flag 4) every active object that isn't type 2/3.

0x8F8.name: set_node_rotation
0x8F8.desc: Gives the object's render instance a node override controller (+0x2C4) for the model node named 'node' (archive hash) with the given vector - Mission 3 turns its RADARDISH this way.

0x900.name: remove_vehicles_in_region
0x900.desc: Takes every type-0 object (vehicles / props) whose position is inside the region out of play (FUN_004c93a0: in-play bit cleared, hidden, moved to the inactive list).

0x904.name: remove_corpses_in_region
0x904.desc: 0x440060: region by index ([0x6800F8] 0x515940); corpse manager [0x641614] 0x46F7C0: each of its 6 in-play corpse holders (+0x24 array) whose render position is inside the region (0x5158E0) is taken out of play (vtable +8(0)). Same as DS1 0x844 (FUN_0041B4F0, which uses FUN_004C93A0). Mission01.

0x908.name: tint_soldier_red
0x908.desc: FUN_00436b10: applies colour (0.5, 0, 0, 1) with value 15.0 to the soldier's skinned mesh (FUN_005019f0 -> 0x528990) - likely a blood / damage tint.

0x90C.name: has_startup_flag
0x90C.desc: FUN_004b9cd0: 1 if the start-up option letter is set (Training 3 checks 'u', the dev movie-skip flag).

0x918.name: set_squad_banter
0x918.desc: Sets [0x5E91F4] (1 by default): enables squad idle speech 0xFD8 when a squad mate is near and in view (FUN_0042af80). Training 3 only.

0x91C.name: set_flag_5f5678
0x91C.desc: Sets [0x5F5678] (equipment ctor sets 1): when on, equipment items get +0x64 = 1 (FUN_004a4a10). Training 3 only; meaning unclear.

0x920.name: set_auto_target_assist
0x920.desc: Sets [0x5F567C]: enables FUN_00435760 (the player's soldier picks a nearby / aimed combat soldier within 2 m as a target) and an inventory check at 0x45335D. Mission 1 turns it off then on; Training 3 too.

0x958.name: allow_stance_0
0x958.desc: Sets [0x5F5668]: while 0, soldiers can't switch to stance 0 (FUN_0045cf00 refuses). Training 1/3 use it to unlock a stance (probably prone/crouch) for the tutorial.

0x95C.name: get_local_player_count
0x95C.desc: Returns 1 on PC (DS1 0x8A8, which DesertStormFix's co-op scripts answer with the player count).

0x960.name: set_head_tracking_off
0x960.desc: 0x43FF60: soldier +0x105C |= 0x400000. While set the head-look update in 0x47B970 skips the blend towards the look target and zeroes the head angles +0x30C..+0x314 every frame (what it does for everyone during a cinematic, [0x68008C]+0x1B8C bit 0) - the soldier looks straight ahead. Counterpart 0x964. Mission02.
0x960.lua_hint: DS1 does this only for all soldiers during cinematics (+0x8AC / +0x8B0, flag [0x60F20C], code 0x42E4CF). Per soldier: zero DS1 soldier view / head angles (+0x310..) each frame from Lua while the flag is on, or ignore (cosmetic).

0x964.name: set_head_tracking_on
0x964.desc: 0x43FF80: clears soldier +0x105C bit 0x400000 (see 0x960) - head looks at targets again.

0x96C.name: get_value_8c0
0x96C.desc: Returns **(handle+0x18) as a float (FUN_004d0e30), 0.0 for a null handle; 0x8C4 is the matching setter. Mission 12B doubles the result.

0x978.name: spawn_debris_at_waypoint
0x978.desc: Spawns a particle / debris burst of effect type (table [0x63C9C8], index & 0x3FF; FUN_0054c5c0) at waypoint n's position / direction ([0x63C9B0], 0x20-byte entries). Mission 1 uses waypoints 0x154-0x15D with type 0x2C (explosions).

0x97C.name: set_view_camera
0x97C.desc: Makes camera n the active camera of view / viewport v (camera manager FUN_004d4f80), resets the view controller; for camera != 0 also starts a ramp (1.0 -> 5.0) on timer [0x63C954].

0x980.name: get_soldier_view
0x980.desc: Returns the viewport index (+0x474 of the controlling input block +0x23C0) of a player-controlled soldier, -1 if no player drives it.

0x9B8.name: set_music_fade_time
0x9B8.desc: Sound manager [0x6800EC] +0x28 = (target - +0x24) / time: the music volume's fade rate.

0x9C4.name: holster
0x9C4.desc: For a soldier (+4 = 1): hold nothing - 0x47EFF0(0) (the held-item switch: +0x6CC, sounds, animations). Desert Storm's hold_item (+0x5CC) with -1 does the same.

0x9D0.name: random_int
0x9D0.desc: 0x4457A0 jmp 0x4BD5C0 (cdecl): next dword of the game's 2048-entry random table (0x65B748, index 0x65F74C) modulo n; 0 when n = 0. NOT a key-frame animation call (the catalogue guess is wrong). Sites: random(2) choices, random(0x14), delays random(0xFA0) / random(0xAFC8) ms; 41 calls.
0x9D0.lua_hint: DS1 has the same helper without a slot: x86rt cdecl call 0x4B7E60(n) (int table 0x619FE0, index 0x61DFE8) - keeps online / determinism runs in step (seeded by the lockstep reseed); guard n = 0 (DS1's divides by zero).

0x9D4.name: register_lipsync_anims
0x9D4.desc: 0x43FE50: list of 12-byte entries {int sound id (< 0 ends), char* key-frame anim name, out handle}: each name is loaded through the key-frame animation manager [0x6800A4] (0x565910; 'Failed to load key frame anim "%s"' if missing), the handle stored at +8, and the list pointer kept in [0x634BF8]. 0x43FDE0(sound) looks a sound up there: the soldier sound slots (0x890/0x894/0x89C/0x8A0) play that facial animation as lip sync. Mission02 registers 5 speech ids -> 'FaceTalk.kan'.
0x9D4.lua_hint: DS1 has no facial / key-frame animation: make it a no-op (lip sync is cosmetic). Could be faked only with a DS1 head animation layer, not worth it.

0x9D8.name: set_split_views_enabled
0x9D8.desc: 0x4428E0: [0x62F3A8] = on (level init 0x412690 sets 1). Read by the render loop (0x40DBC0, 0x40FD10): outside cinematics and certain front-end states, 0 = only the first player's view is rendered, full screen (renderer +0x41A00 viewport, the per-player loop stops after player 1); 1 = each player gets its own viewport (0x536BB0(i)). Missions 1/2/3/7/9 switch it off around scripted sequences and back on.
0x9D8.lua_hint: DS1 renders cutscenes full screen by itself (FUN_0040E080 = 0 while the cinematic bit is set), so a no-op is fine for scripted films; for non-cinematic use DesertStormFix's split-screen code would need a 'one view' switch.

0x9E8.name: set_fixed_bump_lighting
0x9E8.desc: 0x4457E0: renderer [0x680038] +0x20 = kind1, +0x24 = kind0, +0x28 = intensity (level init 0x412690 zeroes them). Read by 0x553210 / 0x553730, the per-instance light used for DOT3 bump mapping (instance byte +0x144 = light kind; callers 0x4D316A, 0x560A5C): for a kind whose flag is 1 the strength is the fixed intensity instead of the time-of-day value (atmosphere [0x68008C]+0x1A4C +0x3C hour) and the direction a fixed vector ([0x61C88C]) instead of the scene light's. Missions 1 and 4 call (0, 1, 0.35) at set-up in single player only (after 0x95C <= 1).
0x9E8.lua_hint: Cosmetic; DS1's bump lighting follows its own sun keys - no-op.
